summary.intent: Finish work package W in the callisto repo: fix `status` spawning O(T) git processes when many foreign tags sit on one commit, then validate with mutation testing, push the branch and link trail #462.
summary.outcome: The fix is committed. `status` now starts 17 git processes at any tag count, down from 6T+4, and the lint, doc-check, pre-push and test recipes passed. A first mutation run exposed a coverage gap, so a regression test was added and committed and mutation testing was re-launched. The final mutation result, the push of `HEAD:refs/heads/worktree-wp-w-history-cache`, the `ls-remote` check and the trail link were still pending.

repo: Tag ownership across ecosystems is decided in crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs. `rank_tags` parses and orders candidates once, and `select_last_tag` wraps it.
After the first rejected tag, the remaining tags are probed by commit, so tags on the same commit share one set of probes. Literal-name ownership from work package E is preserved.
A cascade test expects only a `tag --list` call from `status`, so commit reads must be lazy and happen only after a rejection.
The bench has a `foreign tags` shape. Process counts for ordinary Cargo and pnpm workspaces are unchanged at 8, 16 and 11.
Repo checks are run with `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test`.

Test fixtures come from `callisto_fixtures::git::init_repo` and `GitRunner`. Workspaces are built with `crate::locate::IgnoreWalkLocator` and `Workspace::load`, and the tag index comes from `ws.tags()`.
The work is on worktree branch `worktree-wp-w-history-cache`. Mutation testing is run by a script at ~/.claude/jobs/3d27cecb/tmp/mut_w.sh.

code.finding: A new test `all_tags_made_on_one_commit_by_another_package_are_foreign` pins that every tag of a commit that held the name in another ecosystem is rejected, not only the newest. It asserts `last_tag` is None and `is_tag_of` is false for each tag. It was added after the first mutation run.

workflow: Reading git commits lazily, only after the first rejection, avoided adding a process to every workspace. The eager first version did that and also broke an existing test.
Process-count and wall-time measurements at several sizes (T = 10, 50, 200) confirmed the 6T+4 growth and the flat 17 after the fix.
Mutation testing found a gap that the existing tests missed, and a targeted regression test closed it. The mutation run then had to be repeated.
Slow cargo runs are kept light with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 and debug info disabled for the dev and test profiles.
Long mutation runs go in the background and their output is read from the task output file once they finish.
